title: Boids: Flocking Simulation
description: Simple local rules — separation, alignment, cohesion — produce realistic flocking behavior. Based on Craig Reynolds' 1987 model.

title: Hare & Lynx: Predator–Prey Cycles
description: Every dot is one animal grazing, hunting and breeding on its own energy budget — and the boom-and-bust population cycles emerge from those simple rules.

title: Conway's Game of Life
description: One simple rule about live and dead neighbors gives rise to gliders, oscillators, and endlessly complex patterns.

title: Traffic Jams
description: See how traffic jams form out of nowhere on a road with no obstacles, purely from car-following dynamics.

title: Schelling's Segregation Model
description: Mild individual preferences for similar neighbors add up to strong citywide segregation — a classic result in social science.

title: Double Pendulum: Chaos
description: A perfectly deterministic system whose motion becomes unpredictable — the clearest visual introduction to chaos theory.

title: Epidemic Spread (SIR)
description: Susceptible, infected, and recovered agents wander and mix — tune infection rate and recovery time to see outbreaks burn out or explode.

title: Lorenz Attractor
description: The original chaotic system — a butterfly-shaped trajectory that never repeats, from a simplified model of atmospheric convection.

title: N-Body Gravity
description: Bodies pulling on each other with Newtonian gravity — click to drop in new masses and watch orbits, captures, and ejections unfold.

title: Reaction-Diffusion
description: Two chemicals diffusing and reacting (Gray-Scott model) spontaneously form spots, stripes, and coral-like patterns — click presets or paint your own seeds.

title: Pharmacokinetics
description: Explore how drug concentration in the body changes over time under different dosing regimens.
